Right now the site can't know about a cancellation. The page is built from `sailings.csv`, which the ferry office exports each night, and nothing in that file marks a sailing as cancelled. So the first thing to settle is where that information will come from.

Timing matters most here. Many cancellations happen on the day, for weather or a broken-down boat. A nightly file would not show those until the next morning, which is too late. If cancellations are mostly planned in advance, a new column in the nightly export could be enough. If they happen on the day, someone needs a faster way to post them, and that is a bigger build.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The app only reads data. It turns one nightly file into one page, so it has no place to store an update made during the day.
- Any same-day warning means the app needs a second source of truth next to the CSV. That source also needs a rule for which one wins when they disagree.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

When a sailing is cancelled today, how does the ferry office find out, and how do they tell passengers now?

Or if you'd rather I just dive in, say so.
